_comment: Settings for dailybrief.py. Edit and save -- changes take effect on the next run.
_engine: local = keyless APIs only, no credentials, no cost (default). claude = same data, but Claude writes the prose (needs a signed-in CLI or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). auto = claude if a credential exists, else local.
_location: Set EITHER city (with country to disambiguate) OR postcode. Edit one and the coordinates re-resolve automatically on the next run. To pin exact coordinates instead, clear city and postcode and set latitude/longitude yourself. `label` and `resolved_from` are written by the program -- do not edit them by hand.
_units: temperature: celsius | fahrenheit. wind: mph | kmh | ms | kn. precipitation: mm | inch. clock: 24h | 12h. Anything unrecognised falls back to metric.
_bank_holiday_division: Set automatically from your location: england-and-wales | scotland | northern-ireland. Scotland's calendar genuinely differs.
_sections: Which sections render. Built-ins: weather, tech, onthisday, bankholiday. Any other name here is a feed section drawn from `feeds` below. `sources add` keeps this in step for you.
_feeds: Manage with `dailybrief.py sources list|add|edit|remove|enable|disable|test` -- `add` fetches and parses the feed before saving, so a dead source cannot be added silently. Editing by hand works too. Each entry: name, url, section (the heading it appears under), max_items, max_age_hours (items older than this are ignored), enabled. Reuters and AP RSS are DEAD; CNN returns 200 but has been frozen since 2023.
_section_titles: Override a section heading, e.g. {"audio": "Audio & DSP"}. Sensible defaults exist for news, tech, audio, sport, science and local.
_browser: "auto" picks Edge/Chrome for a chromeless app window; "default" uses your default browser; or give a full path to an exe.
_claude: Only used when engine is claude/auto. Tools are empty because the data is already fetched -- Claude writes, it does not research.
